request.prompt:
Use your built-in image generation tool to create ONE square 1024x1024 image. The first 4 attached images are STYLE references only (frame, flat shapes, palette); do not copy their birds. Save the generated PNG into the current working directory as out.png and reply with only its path. This is variation 1; vary the composition a little. Image brief:
Flat geometric bird icon in a Mondrian / De Stijl spirit, matching the reference images. A thick navy square frame (#0B0F24) around an ivory field (#FAF6EE). Right-facing head-and-upper-breast portrait (owls may face straight ahead). The bird is a bold navy silhouette with a few flat color fields; it may run off the bottom and left edges of the frame only, and leaves clear ivory space between the bill tip, crest and the frame. One simple round eye. Use only these colors: navy #0B0F24, ivory #FAF6EE, chrome yellow #F7B902, vermilion #C7301C, Klein blue #002FA7, slate #5E6178. Three or four colors in total. No gradients, shading, texture, outlines of feather detail, scenery, text or labels. Simple shapes that stay readable at 32 pixels.

Species: American Kestrel (Falco sparverius). Identifying features to show: two dark vertical face stripes: one below the eye, one behind it on the ear; blue-grey crown with a small rufous spot; white cheeks and throat; rufous nape and back; yellow eye-ring and cere; small hooked bill. Proportions measured from a photo: bill to head = 0.25. Do not draw: only one face stripe; large or long bill; a crest; toucan-like shapes.
Art director's change for this version: No Klein blue anywhere. Exactly two dark vertical face stripes: one below the eye, one behind it on the ear. A slate-grey crown (slate #5E6178) with a small rufous spot, white cheeks and throat, rufous nape and back, a yellow eye-ring and a small hooked bill.
